brief: Morgan Stanley shifts its US baseline from benign Middle East de-escalation to an oil risk-premium scenario. Supply chain disruptions (constrained Middle East export routes, pipeline outages, shipping bottlenecks, tight tanker capacity, refinery disruptions, low European fuel inventories) are converging as buffers that previously absorbed shocks (strong US exports, weak Chinese demand, ample inventories) fade, leaving oil vulnerable to further geopolitical disruption. WTI and Brent have risen to $107.02 and $130.80 per barrel, and the SPR has fallen to its lowest level since April 1984. Persistently higher oil prices are expected to produce second-round inflation effects, delaying the airfare disinflation MS previously assumed. MS raises its core PCE forecast to 3.2% (2026) and 2.7% (2027), trims 2027 real GDP to 2.3% (from 2.6%), consumption to 1.8% (from 2.1%), and nonresidential investment growth to 7.1%, while trimming payroll growth to 50k/month and raising unemployment to 4.3%. In response, MS now expects two more 25bp Fed hikes (December, March) to a 4.25-4.50% terminal rate, citing Chair Warsh's hawkish September comments and an upward revision to the FOMC's neutral-rate estimate. MS assigns this oil risk-premium baseline a 45% probability.
